chapters.title: Nebuchadnezzar and Arphaxad
chapters.html:
Judith 1

The War against Arphaxad

1In the twelfth year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, who reigned over the Assyrians in the great city of Nineveh, in the days of Arphaxad, who reigned over the Medes in Ecbatana,

2this Arphaxad built walls around Ecbatana of hewn stones three cubits wide and six cubits long. He made the walls seventy cubits high and fifty cubits wide.

3At its gates he set towers a hundred cubits high, and he laid their foundations sixty cubits wide.

4He made its gates, gates that rose to a height of seventy cubits and were forty cubits wide, for the marching out of his mighty forces and the drawing up of his foot soldiers.

5In those days King Nebuchadnezzar made war against King Arphaxad in the great plain, which is in the region of Ragau.

6There came to meet him all who lived in the hill country and all who lived along the Euphrates, the Tigris and the Hydaspes, and in the plain Arioch king of the Elymaeans. Many nations joined the ranks of the sons of Cheleoul.

The Nations Refuse

7Then Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians sent to all who lived in Persia and to all who lived in the west, to those who lived in Cilicia and Damascus, Lebanon and Antilebanon, and to all who lived along the seacoast,

8and to those among the nations of Carmel and Gilead, and to Upper Galilee and the great plain of Esdraelon,

9and to all who were in Samaria and its towns, and beyond the Jordan as far as Jerusalem, Bethany, Chelous and Kadesh, and the river of Egypt, Tahpanhes, Raamses and all the land of Goshen,

10until one comes beyond Tanis and Memphis, and to all who lived in Egypt as far as the borders of Ethiopia.

11But all who lived in the whole land made light of the summons of Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians and did not join him in the war. They were not afraid of him, but looked on him as a man like themselves, and they sent his messengers back empty-handed and in disgrace.

12Nebuchadnezzar was furious with all this land, and he swore by his throne and his kingdom that he would take vengeance on all the territory of Cilicia, Damascus and Syria, and would kill with his sword all who lived in the land of Moab, the sons of Ammon, all Judea and all who were in Egypt, as far as the borders of the two seas.

The Defeat of Arphaxad

13In the seventeenth year he drew up his forces against King Arphaxad and prevailed in the battle. He overthrew all the army of Arphaxad, all his cavalry and all his chariots,

14and became master of his cities. He came as far as Ecbatana, took its towers, plundered its streets and turned its beauty into shame.

15He captured Arphaxad in the mountains of Ragau, struck him through with his hunting spears and destroyed him once and for all.

16Then he returned with them, he and his army, for a hundred and twenty days.

Notes

  • v1 "Nebuchadnezzar, who reigned over the Assyrians in the great city of Nineveh" — Kings and Chronicles know Nebuchadnezzar as king of Babylon (2 Kings 24:1), and Nineveh as the city whose fall Tobias lived to hear of (Tobit 14:15). The book sets its story in a world where the great enemies of Israel are joined into one king.

  • v1 "Arphaxad, who reigned over the Medes" — the name of a son of Shem (Genesis 10:22). He is known nowhere else as a king.

  • vv2–4 "seventy cubits high and fifty cubits wide… towers a hundred cubits high" — the walls of the city that will fall in v14. The more the numbers grow, the greater the king who takes it.

  • v6 "Arioch king of the Elymaeans" — a name from the war of the four kings, Arioch king of Ellasar (Genesis 14:1).

  • v11 "looked on him as a man like themselves" — hōs anēr isos, as an equal man. The book is about who is God and who is a man; the nations do not yet fear him.

  • v12 "he swore by his throne and his kingdom" — the king swears by himself. Its counterpart is his title in the next chapter, the lord of the whole earth (2:5).

chapters.title: Holofernes Sent to the West
chapters.html:
Judith 2

The King's Command

1In the eighteenth year, on the twenty-second day of the first month, word went out in the house of Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians that he would take vengeance on all the land, as he had said.

2He called together all his officials and all his nobles and set before them his secret plan, and with his own mouth he decreed all the evil to be done to the land.

3They decided to destroy all flesh that had not obeyed the word of his mouth.

4When he had finished setting out his plan, Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians called Holofernes, the commander in chief of his army, who was second only to himself, and said to him,

5"Thus says the great king, the lord of the whole earth: You shall go out from my presence and take with you men confident in their strength, a hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers and a body of horses with their riders, twelve thousand.

6You shall go out against all the land to the west, because they disobeyed the word of my mouth.

7Tell them to prepare earth and water, for I will go out against them in my anger. I will cover the whole face of the earth with the feet of my army, and I will give them to my army to plunder.

8Their wounded will fill their ravines and their streams, and a river will overflow, filled with their dead.

9I will lead their captives away to the ends of the whole earth.

10You shall go ahead of me and seize all their territory for me. They will surrender themselves to you, and you shall hold them for me until the day of their punishment.

11But on those who disobey, your eye shall have no pity; give them up to slaughter and plunder in all the land you hold.

12For as I live, and by the power of my kingdom, I have spoken, and I will do these things by my hand.

13As for you, do not disobey a single word of your lord, but carry it out fully, as I have commanded you, and do not delay in doing it."

The March

14So Holofernes went out from the presence of his lord and called all the commanders, the generals and the officers of the army of Assyria,

15and he mustered picked men for battle, as his lord had commanded him, a hundred and twenty thousand, and twelve thousand mounted archers,

16and he organized them as a great army is drawn up for war.

17He took camels, donkeys and mules for their baggage, a very great number, and sheep, oxen and goats without number for their provision,

18and plenty of food for every man, and a great deal of gold and silver from the king's house.

19Then he set out with all his army to go ahead of King Nebuchadnezzar and to cover the whole face of the earth to the west with their chariots, horsemen and picked foot soldiers.

20A mixed crowd as many as locusts went out with them, like the sand of the earth, for they could not be counted for their multitude.

21They marched three days from Nineveh toward the plain of Bectileth, and camped from Bectileth near the mountain that is to the left of Upper Cilicia.

22From there he took all his army, his foot soldiers, horsemen and chariots, and went up into the hill country.

23He cut through Put and Lud, and plundered all the sons of Rassis and the sons of Ishmael who lived along the desert, south of the land of the Chaldeans.

24He crossed the Euphrates and went through Mesopotamia, and destroyed all the fortified cities along the brook Abron, as far as the sea.

25He seized the territory of Cilicia and cut down all who resisted him, and came to the borders of Japheth, toward the south, facing Arabia.

26He surrounded all the sons of Midian, burned their tents and plundered their sheepfolds.

27He went down into the plain of Damascus at the time of the wheat harvest, set fire to all their fields, destroyed their flocks and herds, looted their towns, swept their plains bare and struck down all their young men with the edge of the sword.

Fear on the Coast

28Fear and trembling of him fell on all who lived along the seacoast, those in Sidon and Tyre, those who lived in Sur and Ocina, and all who lived in Jamnia. Those who lived in Azotus and Ascalon feared him greatly.

Notes

  • v5 "Thus says the great king, the lord of the whole earth" — the words of the prophets, Thus says the LORD, in the mouth of a king who claims the earth. The Rabshakeh spoke so for Sennacherib: Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria (2 Kings 18:19). The question of the book is whose title it is.

  • v7 "Tell them to prepare earth and water" — the tokens of a land's surrender: its soil and its water handed over to the conqueror.

  • v12 "For as I live… I have spoken, and I will do these things" — the oath of the LORD in the prophets, As I live, declares the Lord GOD (Ezekiel 33:11), and I the LORD have spoken, and I will do it (Ezekiel 36:36), here sworn by a man.

  • v20 "as many as locusts… like the sand of the earth" — the armies of Midian in the days of Gideon, as many as locusts… their camels without number, as the sand on the seashore (Judges 7:12).

  • v23 "Put and Lud" — peoples named in the table of nations (Genesis 10:6, 22). Many of the places in the march are not known elsewhere.

chapters.title: The Coast Surrenders
chapters.html:
Judith 3

The Offer of Peace

1So they sent messengers to him with words of peace, saying,

2"We, the servants of Nebuchadnezzar the great king, lie before you. Do with us as seems good to you.

3Our farmsteads, all our wheat fields, our flocks and herds and all the sheepfolds of our tents lie before you. Do with them as you please.

4Our cities also and those who live in them are your slaves. Come and deal with them as seems good in your eyes."

5The men came to Holofernes and reported these words to him.

The Gods Destroyed

6Then he came down to the seacoast with his army and put garrisons in the fortified cities, and took picked men from them as auxiliaries.

7They and all the country around welcomed him with garlands and dancing and tambourines.

8Yet he demolished all their territory and cut down their sacred groves, for it had been given to him to destroy all the gods of the land, so that all the nations would worship Nebuchadnezzar alone, and all their tongues and tribes would call on him as god.

9Then he came toward Esdraelon, near Dothan, which faces the great ridge of Judea,

10and they camped between Geba and Scythopolis, and he stayed there a whole month to gather all the baggage of his army.

Notes

  • vv2–4 "lie before you… Do with us as seems good to you" — the coastal cities surrender before they are attacked, in the words of a slave to a master.

  • v7 "with garlands and dancing and tambourines" — the welcome Israel's women gave to a victor, with tambourines and dancing (1 Samuel 18:6), given here to the destroyer.

  • v8 "to destroy all the gods of the land, so that all the nations would worship Nebuchadnezzar alone… call on him as god" — the claim the book is built to answer. Daniel's Nebuchadnezzar sets up an image for all peoples, nations and languages to worship (Daniel 3:4–5).

  • v9 "near Dothan, which faces the great ridge of Judea" — priōn, a saw: the jagged line of the hills. Dothan is where Joseph's brothers sold him (Genesis 37:17) and where Elisha's servant saw the hills full of horses and chariots of fire (2 Kings 6:13–17).

chapters.title: Israel Prepares and Prays
chapters.html:
Judith 4

Fear in Judea

1The sons of Israel who lived in Judea heard all that Holofernes, the commander in chief of Nebuchadnezzar king of the Assyrians, had done to the nations, and how he had plundered all their temples and given them up to destruction.

2They were terrified of him, and they were alarmed for Jerusalem and for the temple of the Lord their God.

3For they had only lately come up from the captivity, and all the people of Judea had only just been gathered together, and the vessels, the altar and the house had been consecrated after their profanation.

The Passes Held

4So they sent word to every region of Samaria, and to Kona, Beth-horon, Belmain and Jericho, and to Choba, Aesora and the valley of Salem,

5and they occupied all the tops of the high mountains, fortified the villages on them and stored up food in preparation for war, for their fields had just been harvested.

6Joakim the high priest, who was in Jerusalem in those days, wrote to those who lived in Bethulia and Betomesthaim, which faces Esdraelon opposite the plain near Dothan,

7telling them to hold the passes into the hill country, since through them was the way into Judea. It was easy to stop any who tried to come up, because the approach was narrow, wide enough for two men at most.

8The sons of Israel did as Joakim the high priest and the council of the whole people of Israel, sitting in Jerusalem, had commanded them.

The Cry to God

9Every man of Israel cried out to God with great fervor, and they humbled themselves with great fervor,

10they and their wives and their little children and their cattle. Every guest, hired worker and purchased slave put sackcloth around his waist.

11All the men, women and children of Israel who lived in Jerusalem fell down before the temple, put ashes on their heads and spread out their sackcloth before the Lord.

12They even draped the altar in sackcloth, and they cried out with one accord and fervently to the God of Israel, not to give up their little children to be seized, or their wives to be carried off, or the cities of their inheritance to be destroyed, or the sanctuary to be profaned and mocked, a thing for the nations to gloat over.

13The Lord heard their voice and looked on their distress. The people fasted many days in all Judea and in Jerusalem before the sanctuary of the Lord Almighty.

14Joakim the high priest and all the priests who stood before the Lord and ministered to the Lord, with sackcloth around their waists, offered the continual burnt offering and the vows and the freewill offerings of the people,

15with ashes on their turbans, and they cried out to the Lord with all their might to look with favor on the whole house of Israel.

Notes

  • v3 "they had only lately come up from the captivity… the house had been consecrated after their profanation" — the book's Israel has returned and rebuilt, as in Ezra and Nehemiah, and now fears for the house just made holy again.

  • v7 "wide enough for two men at most" — the whole land's defense rests on narrow passes held by one town, Bethulia, where the story will stay.

  • vv9–10 "they humbled themselves… they and their wives and their little children and their cattle" — as Nineveh fasted at Jonah's word: let man and beast be covered with sackcloth (Jonah 3:8).

  • v10 "Every guest, hired worker and purchased slave" — paroikos, the Greek for ger, the guest of the law, joins the fast with Israel.

  • v13 "the Lord Almighty" — Kyrios Pantokratōr, Lord, ruler of all, the Greek for the LORD of hosts. The answer to a king who calls himself lord of the whole earth (2:5).

chapters.title: Achior Tells of Israel
chapters.html:
Judith 5

Holofernes Asks

1It was reported to Holofernes, the commander in chief of the army of Assyria, that the sons of Israel had prepared for war, had shut the passes of the hill country, fortified every high hilltop and set traps in the plains.

2He was furious, and he called all the leaders of Moab, the generals of Ammon and all the governors of the coast,

3and said to them, "Tell me now, you sons of Canaan, who is this people that lives in the hill country? What cities do they live in, how large is their army, and in what does their power and strength lie? Who has risen up as their king and leads their army?

4Why have they refused to come out to meet me, alone of all who live in the west?"

Achior's Answer

5Achior, the leader of all the sons of Ammon, said to him, "Let my lord now hear a word from the mouth of your servant, and I will tell you the truth about this people who live in the hill country near where you are camped. No lie shall come from the mouth of your servant.

6This people is descended from the Chaldeans.

7They once lived as guests in Mesopotamia, because they would not follow the gods of their fathers who were in the land of the Chaldeans.

8They left the way of their ancestors and worshiped the God of heaven, the God they had come to know. So their people drove them out from the presence of their gods, and they fled to Mesopotamia and lived there as guests for many days.

9Then their God told them to leave the place where they were guests and go into the land of Canaan. They settled there and grew rich in gold and silver and in very many cattle.

10When a famine covered the face of the land of Canaan, they went down into Egypt and lived there as guests as long as they had food. There they became a great multitude, so that their race could not be counted.

11But the king of Egypt rose up against them and took advantage of them with hard labor and brickmaking. They humbled them and made them slaves.

12They cried out to their God, and He struck the land of Egypt with plagues for which there was no cure. So the Egyptians drove them out of their sight.

13God dried up the Red Sea before them,

14and led them by the way of Sinai and Kadesh-barnea. They drove out all who lived in the desert,

15and they lived in the land of the Amorites and by their strength destroyed all the people of Heshbon. Then they crossed the Jordan and took possession of all the hill country.

16They drove out before them the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, the people of Shechem and all the Girgashites, and they lived there for many days.

17As long as they did not sin before their God, good things were with them, for a God who hates wrongdoing is with them.

18But when they turned away from the way He had set for them, they were utterly destroyed in many wars and were carried captive to a land not their own. The temple of their God was razed to the ground, and their cities were taken by their enemies.

19But now they have turned back to their God and have come up from the dispersion where they were scattered. They have taken possession of Jerusalem, where their sanctuary is, and have settled in the hill country, because it was empty.

20So now, my master and lord, if there is any error in this people, and they sin against their God, and we find out that they have this offense among them, then we will go up and defeat them.

21But if there is no lawlessness in their nation, let my lord pass them by, or their Lord and God will defend them, and we will be put to shame before the whole earth."

The Anger of the Camp

22When Achior had finished saying these things, all the people standing around the tent murmured, and the nobles of Holofernes and all who lived by the sea and in Moab said he should be cut to pieces.

23"We will not be afraid of the sons of Israel. They are a people with no power or strength for a hard battle.

24So we will go up, master Holofernes, and they will be devoured by your whole army."

Notes

  • v5 "Achior, the leader of all the sons of Ammon" — an Ammonite, of the people the law shuts out of the assembly of the LORD (Deuteronomy 23:3). He is the one in the enemy's camp who tells the truth about Israel's God.

  • vv6–8 "descended from the Chaldeans… they would not follow the gods of their fathers" — Abram came from Ur of the Chaldeans (Genesis 11:31), and Joshua says your fathers… served other gods beyond the river (Joshua 24:2). Achior tells of a family driven out for leaving its fathers' gods.

  • vv7–10 "lived as guests" — paroikeō, the Greek for gur, the verb of the guest (Genesis 12:10; 47:4).

  • vv17–21 "As long as they did not sin before their God, good things were with them" — the whole history in one law: blessing for keeping the way, defeat and exile for leaving it. Achior's advice rests on it: find out whether they have sinned.

  • v21 "their Lord and God will defend them" — hyperaspizō, to hold a shield over. The next chapter's question answers it: Who is God except Nebuchadnezzar? (6:2).

Holofernes Asks

It was reported to Holofernes, the commander in chief of the army of Assyria, that the sons of Israel had prepared for war, had shut the passes of the hill country, fortified every high hilltop and set traps in the plains.
He was furious, and he called all the leaders of Moab, the generals of Ammon and all the governors of the coast,

and said to them, "Tell me now, you sons of Canaan, who is this people that lives in the hill country? What cities do they live in, how large is their army, and in what does their power and strength lie? Who has risen up as their king and leads their army?
Why have they refused to come out to meet me, alone of all who live in the west?"
Achior's Answer

Achior, the leader of all the sons of Ammon, said to him, "Let my lord now hear a word from the mouth of your servant, and I will tell you the truth about this people who live in the hill country near where you are camped. No lie shall come from the mouth of your servant.
This people is descended from the Chaldeans.
They once lived as guests in Mesopotamia, because they would not follow the gods of their fathers who were in the land of the Chaldeans.

They left the way of their ancestors and worshiped the God of heaven, the God they had come to know. So their people drove them out from the presence of their gods, and they fled to Mesopotamia and lived there as guests for many days.
Then their God told them to leave the place where they were guests and go into the land of Canaan. They settled there and grew rich in gold and silver and in very many cattle.

When a famine covered the face of the land of Canaan, they went down into Egypt and lived there as guests as long as they had food. There they became a great multitude, so that their race could not be counted.
But the king of Egypt rose up against them and took advantage of them with hard labor and brickmaking. They humbled them and made them slaves.
They cried out to their God, and He struck the land of Egypt with plagues for which there was no cure. So the Egyptians drove them out of their sight.
God dried up the Red Sea before them,
and led them by the way of Sinai and Kadesh-barnea. They drove out all who lived in the desert,
and they lived in the land of the Amorites and by their strength destroyed all the people of Heshbon. Then they crossed the Jordan and took possession of all the hill country.
They drove out before them the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, the people of Shechem and all the Girgashites, and they lived there for many days.
As long as they did not sin before their God, good things were with them, for a God who hates wrongdoing is with them.

But when they turned away from the way He had set for them, they were utterly destroyed in many wars and were carried captive to a land not their own. The temple of their God was razed to the ground, and their cities were taken by their enemies.

But now they have turned back to their God and have come up from the dispersion where they were scattered. They have taken possession of Jerusalem, where their sanctuary is, and have settled in the hill country, because it was empty.
So now, my master and lord, if there is any error in this people, and they sin against their God, and we find out that they have this offense among them, then we will go up and defeat them.
But if there is no lawlessness in their nation, let my lord pass them by, or their Lord and God will defend them, and we will be put to shame before the whole earth."
The Anger of the Camp
When Achior had finished saying these things, all the people standing around the tent murmured, and the nobles of Holofernes and all who lived by the sea and in Moab said he should be cut to pieces.
"We will not be afraid of the sons of Israel. They are a people with no power or strength for a hard battle.
So we will go up, master Holofernes, and they will be devoured by your whole army."

chapters.title: Achior Handed Over
chapters.html:
Judith 6

"Who Is God Except Nebuchadnezzar?"

1When the uproar of the men around the council had died down, Holofernes, the commander in chief of the army of Assyria, said to Achior in front of the whole crowd of foreigners,

2"Who are you, Achior, you and the hirelings of Ephraim, to prophesy among us as you have today, and to tell us not to make war on the race of Israel because their God will defend them? Who is God except Nebuchadnezzar? He will send his power and destroy them from the face of the earth, and their God will not deliver them.

3We his servants will strike them down as one man. They will not withstand the might of our horses.

4We will burn them up in their own land. Their mountains will be drunk with their blood, and their plains will be filled with their dead. They will not be able to stand their ground before us, but will utterly perish, says King Nebuchadnezzar, the lord of the whole earth. For he has spoken; none of his words will be in vain.

5As for you, Achior, you hireling of Ammon, who have spoken these words in the day of your wrongdoing, you will not see my face again from this day until I take vengeance on this race that came out of Egypt.

6Then the iron of my army and the people of my servants will pierce your sides, and you will fall among their wounded when I return.

7My servants will take you back into the hill country and leave you in one of the cities along the passes,

8and you will not die until you are destroyed with them.

9If you really hope in your heart that they will not be taken, then do not look so downcast. I have spoken, and none of my words will fail."

Achior at Bethulia

10Then Holofernes ordered his servants who stood in his tent to seize Achior and take him back to Bethulia and hand him over to the sons of Israel.

11So his servants seized him and took him out of the camp into the plain, and from the plain they went up into the hill country and came to the springs below Bethulia.

12When the men of the city saw them on the top of the hill, they took up their weapons and went out of the city to the top of the hill, and all the slingers kept them from coming up by throwing stones at them.

13So they slipped down under the hill, bound Achior and left him lying at the foot of the hill, and went back to their lord.

14Then the sons of Israel came down from their city and stood over him. They untied him and brought him into Bethulia and set him before the rulers of their city,

15who in those days were Uzziah son of Micah, of the tribe of Simeon, Chabris son of Gothoniel, and Charmis son of Melchiel.

16They called together all the elders of the city, and all their young men and their women ran to the assembly. They set Achior in the middle of all their people, and Uzziah asked him what had happened.

17He answered and told them what had been said in the council of Holofernes, and all that he himself had said among the leaders of the sons of Assyria, and all the boasts Holofernes had made against the house of Israel.

18Then the people fell down and worshiped God, and cried out,

19"O Lord God of heaven, see their arrogance, and have pity on the lowliness of our race, and look today on the faces of those who are consecrated to You."

20Then they reassured Achior and praised him highly.

21Uzziah took him from the assembly to his house and gave a banquet for the elders, and all that night they called on the God of Israel for help.

Notes

  • v2 "Who is God except Nebuchadnezzar?" — the book's question, asked outright. The words echo the psalm, For who is God except the LORD? (Psalm 18:31), with a king's name put in the LORD's place.

  • v4 "says King Nebuchadnezzar… For he has spoken; none of his words will be in vain" — the speech of a prophet for his god: Thus says… I have spoken (2:12).

  • vv5–8 "you will not see my face again… until you are destroyed with them" — Holofernes sends Achior to share Israel's fate. The next time Achior sees that face, it is a severed head in Bethulia (14:6).

  • v15 "Uzziah son of Micah, of the tribe of Simeon" — Judith too is of Simeon (9:2), the tribe of the brother who avenged Dinah.

  • v19 "look today on the faces of those who are consecrated to You" — set against their arrogance: the prayer asks God to compare the two.

chapters.title: The Siege of Bethulia
chapters.html:
Judith 7

The Army Moves on Bethulia

1The next day Holofernes ordered all his army and all the people who had come to join him as allies to break camp against Bethulia, to seize the passes into the hill country and to make war on the sons of Israel.

2That day all their fighting men broke camp. Their force of warriors was a hundred and seventy thousand foot soldiers and twelve thousand horsemen, not counting the baggage and the men on foot who handled it, a very great multitude.

3They camped in the valley near Bethulia, beside the spring, and spread out in breadth over Dothan as far as Belbaim, and in length from Bethulia to Cyamon, which faces Esdraelon.

4When the sons of Israel saw their multitude, they were greatly alarmed, and they said to one another, "Now these men will lick up the face of the whole land. Neither the high mountains nor the ravines nor the hills will bear their weight."

5Each man took up his weapons, and they lit fires on their towers and stayed on guard all that night.

The Springs Seized

6On the second day Holofernes led out all his cavalry in view of the sons of Israel who were in Bethulia.

7He examined the approaches to their city, visited the springs of water and seized them, and set guards of soldiers over them. Then he went back to his own people.

8All the rulers of the sons of Esau, all the leaders of the people of Moab and the generals of the coast came to him and said,

9"Let our master hear a word, so that no loss may come to your army.

10For this people, the sons of Israel, do not rely on their spears but on the heights of the mountains where they live, because it is not easy to reach the tops of their mountains.

11So now, master, do not fight against them in battle array, and not one man of your army will fall.

12Stay in your camp and keep every man of your army safe, and let your servants take possession of the spring of water that flows from the foot of the mountain,

13for all who live in Bethulia draw their water from there. Thirst will destroy them, and they will give up their city. We and our people will go up to the nearby mountaintops and camp on them as an outpost, so that not one man gets out of the city.

14They and their wives and children will waste away with hunger, and before the sword reaches them they will be strewn about in the streets where they live.

15So you will pay them back with an evil reward, because they rebelled and did not come out to meet you in peace."

16Their words pleased Holofernes and all his servants, and he gave orders to do as they had said.

17So the army of the sons of Ammon moved out, and with them five thousand Assyrians, and they camped in the valley and seized the water supply and the springs of the sons of Israel.

18The sons of Esau and the sons of Ammon went up and camped in the hill country opposite Dothan, and they sent some of their men to the south and the east, opposite Egrebel, which is near Chus beside the brook Mochmur. The rest of the Assyrian army camped in the plain and covered the whole face of the land. Their tents and baggage were spread out in a vast crowd, a very great multitude.

Thirst in the City

19The sons of Israel cried out to the Lord their God, for their spirit failed, because all their enemies had surrounded them and there was no escape from among them.

20The whole army of Assyria, their foot soldiers, chariots and horsemen, remained around them thirty-four days, until all the water jars of everyone who lived in Bethulia were empty.

21Their cisterns were running dry, and they did not have enough water to drink their fill for a single day, because their drink was given them by measure.

22Their little children lost heart, and the women and young men fainted from thirst and fell in the streets of the city and in the gateways. There was no strength left in them.

The People Demand Surrender

23Then all the people, the young men, the women and the children, gathered around Uzziah and the rulers of the city and cried out with a loud voice, and said before all the elders,

24"God judge between you and us! You have done us a great wrong in not making peace with the sons of Assyria.

25Now we have no one to help us. God has sold us into their hands, to be strewn before them in thirst and great destruction.

26Now call them in and surrender the whole city to be plundered by the people of Holofernes and all his army.

27It is better for us to be their spoil. We will be slaves, but we will live, and we will not see our little ones die before our eyes, or our wives and children breathing their last.

28We call to witness against you heaven and earth, and our God, the Lord of our fathers, who punishes us for our sins and the sins of our fathers. Do today what we have said!"

29There was great weeping in the assembly, all with one voice, and they cried out to the Lord God with a loud voice.

30Uzziah said to them, "Take courage, brothers. Let us hold out five more days, in which the Lord our God will turn His mercy to us, for He will not forsake us utterly.

31But if these days pass and no help comes to us, I will do as you say."

32He sent the people away, each to his post, and they went to the walls and towers of their city. He sent the women and children home. They were in great distress in the city.

Notes

  • v4 "Now these men will lick up the face of the whole land" — eklixousin, the picture of Moab's fear of Israel, as the ox licks up the grass of the field (Numbers 22:4). Now Israel is the land about to be licked bare.

  • vv12–13 "take possession of the spring of water… Thirst will destroy them" — the Edomites and Moabites, Israel's own neighbors, teach the Assyrian how to take the town without a battle.

  • v19 "their spirit failed" — ōligopsychēsen, their soul grew small, the word of Israel on the way around Edom, when the soul of the people grew impatient (Numbers 21:4).

  • vv24–28 "You have done us a great wrong… It is better for us to be their spoil" — the cry of the wilderness: Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to kill us… with thirst? (Exodus 17:3). We call to witness against you heaven and earth turns Moses' words against the rulers (Deuteronomy 30:19).

  • vv30–31 "Let us hold out five more days… I will do as you say" — the vow that Judith will rebuke in the next chapter: a deadline set for God.

chapters.title: Judith
chapters.html:
Judith 8

The Widow of Bethulia

1In those days Judith heard of it. She was the daughter of Merari son of Ox, son of Joseph, son of Oziel, son of Elkiah, son of Elijah, son of Hilkiah, son of Eliab, son of Nathanael, son of Salamiel, son of Sarasadai, son of Israel.

2Her husband Manasseh was of her own tribe and family. He had died during the barley harvest.

3For as he stood over the men binding sheaves in the field, the heat came upon his head, and he fell on his bed and died in Bethulia, his town. They buried him with his fathers in the field between Dothan and Balamon.

4Judith had remained a widow in her house three years and four months.

5She made herself a tent on the roof of her house, put sackcloth around her waist and wore the clothes of her widowhood.

6She fasted all the days of her widowhood, except the day before the sabbath and the sabbath, the day before the new moon and the new moon, and the festivals and days of rejoicing of the house of Israel.

7She was beautiful in appearance and very lovely to look at. Her husband Manasseh had left her gold and silver, male and female servants, livestock and fields, and she kept them up.

8No one spoke an evil word against her, for she feared God greatly.

Judith Rebukes the Rulers

9She heard the bitter words of the people against their ruler, because they had lost heart for lack of water, and she heard all that Uzziah had said to them, how he had sworn to surrender the city to the Assyrians after five days.

10So she sent her maid, who was in charge of all she had, and called Chabris and Charmis, the elders of her city.

11They came to her, and she said to them, "Listen to me, rulers of those who live in Bethulia. What you said before the people today is not right. You have sworn this oath, which you have pronounced between God and yourselves, and said you would surrender the city to our enemies unless the Lord turns and helps you within these days.

12Who are you, that you have put God to the test today, and set yourselves up in the place of God among the sons of men?

13You are putting the Lord Almighty to the test, and you will never learn anything.

14You cannot find the depths of a human heart or grasp the thoughts of his mind. How then can you search out God, who made all these things, or know His mind or understand His purpose? No, my brothers, do not provoke the Lord our God to anger.

15For if He does not choose to help us within these five days, He has the power to protect us on any day He wishes, or to destroy us before our enemies.

16Do not try to bind the purposes of the Lord our God, for God is not like a man, to be threatened, nor like a son of man, to be bargained with.

17So while we wait for His deliverance, let us call on Him to help us, and He will hear our voice, if it pleases Him.

18For there has not arisen in our generations, nor is there today, any tribe or family or people or city of ours that worships gods made by hands, as there was in former days.

19It was for that that our fathers were handed over to the sword and to plunder, and fell with a great fall before our enemies.

20But we know no other god but Him. So we hope that He will not despise us or any of our race.

21For if we are taken, all Judea will be taken, and our sanctuary will be plundered, and He will require of our blood its profaning.

22The slaughter of our brothers, the captivity of the land and the desolation of our inheritance He will bring on our heads among the nations wherever we are slaves, and we will be an offense and a reproach in the eyes of those who buy us.

23For our slavery will not bring us into favor; the Lord our God will turn it to dishonor.

24So now, brothers, let us show our brothers that their lives depend on us, and that the sanctuary, the house and the altar rest on us.

25Besides all this, let us give thanks to the Lord our God, who is testing us as He did our fathers.

26Remember what He did with Abraham, how He tested Isaac, and what happened to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria while he was keeping the sheep of Laban, his mother's brother.

27For He has not tried us with fire as He did them, to search their hearts, nor has He taken vengeance on us. The Lord scourges those who draw near to Him, to admonish them."

"I Will Do a Thing"

28Uzziah said to her, "All that you have said you have spoken with a good heart, and no one can deny your words.

29Today is not the first time your wisdom has been shown; from the beginning of your days all the people have known your understanding, for the inclination of your heart is good.

30But the people were very thirsty, and they forced us to do as we told them and to bind ourselves with an oath that we will not break.

31So now pray for us, for you are a devout woman, and the Lord will send rain to fill our cisterns, and we will no longer faint."

32Judith said to them, "Listen to me. I am going to do a thing that will go down through all generations to the sons of our race.

33Stand at the gate tonight, and I will go out with my maid. Within the days after which you said you would surrender the city to our enemies, the Lord will deliver Israel by my hand.

34But do not inquire into what I am doing, for I will not tell you until what I am doing is finished."

35Uzziah and the rulers said to her, "Go in peace, and may the Lord God go before you to take vengeance on our enemies."

36So they left the tent and went back to their posts.

Notes

  • v1 "Judith… son of Salamiel, son of Sarasadai, son of Israel" — Ioudeith, Jewess, the woman of Judah. Her line runs back through Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, the leader of the tribe of Simeon in the wilderness (Numbers 1:6), to Israel himself. Her prayer will name Simeon as her father (9:2).

  • vv2–3 "the heat came upon his head" — as the Shunammite's son went out to his father among the reapers and cried, My head, my head! (2 Kings 4:19).

  • vv12–13 "you have put God to the test" — the law: You shall not put the LORD your God to the test, as you tested Him at Massah (Deuteronomy 6:16), where the people tested Him over water.

  • v16 "God is not like a man, to be threatened, nor like a son of man, to be bargained with" — Balaam's oracle: God is not a man, that He should lie, nor a son of man, that He should change His mind (Numbers 23:19).

  • v27 "The Lord scourges those who draw near to Him, to admonish them" — the proverb, whom the LORD loves He reproves (Proverbs 3:12), and Tobit's song, He scourges and He shows mercy (Tobit 13:2).

  • v33 "the Lord will deliver Israel by my hand" — the word Deborah spoke to Barak: the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman (Judges 4:9).

She heard the bitter words of the people against their ruler, because they had lost heart for lack of water, and she heard all that Uzziah had said to them, how he had sworn to surrender the city to the Assyrians after five days.
So she sent her maid, who was in charge of all she had, and called Chabris and Charmis, the elders of her city.

They came to her, and she said to them, "Listen to me, rulers of those who live in Bethulia. What you said before the people today is not right. You have sworn this oath, which you have pronounced between God and yourselves, and said you would surrender the city to our enemies unless the Lord turns and helps you within these days.
Who are you, that you have put God to the test today, and set yourselves up in the place of God among the sons of men?
You are putting the Lord Almighty to the test, and you will never learn anything.

You cannot find the depths of a human heart or grasp the thoughts of his mind. How then can you search out God, who made all these things, or know His mind or understand His purpose? No, my brothers, do not provoke the Lord our God to anger.
For if He does not choose to help us within these five days, He has the power to protect us on any day He wishes, or to destroy us before our enemies.
Do not try to bind the purposes of the Lord our God, for God is not like a man, to be threatened, nor like a son of man, to be bargained with.
So while we wait for His deliverance, let us call on Him to help us, and He will hear our voice, if it pleases Him.
For there has not arisen in our generations, nor is there today, any tribe or family or people or city of ours that worships gods made by hands, as there was in former days.
It was for that that our fathers were handed over to the sword and to plunder, and fell with a great fall before our enemies.
But we know no other god but Him. So we hope that He will not despise us or any of our race.
For if we are taken, all Judea will be taken, and our sanctuary will be plundered, and He will require of our blood its profaning.

The slaughter of our brothers, the captivity of the land and the desolation of our inheritance He will bring on our heads among the nations wherever we are slaves, and we will be an offense and a reproach in the eyes of those who buy us.
For our slavery will not bring us into favor; the Lord our God will turn it to dishonor.
So now, brothers, let us show our brothers that their lives depend on us, and that the sanctuary, the house and the altar rest on us.
Besides all this, let us give thanks to the Lord our God, who is testing us as He did our fathers.
Remember what He did with Abraham, how He tested Isaac, and what happened to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria while he was keeping the sheep of Laban, his mother's brother.
For He has not tried us with fire as He did them, to search their hearts, nor has He taken vengeance on us. The Lord scourges those who draw near to Him, to admonish them."
"I Will Do a Thing"
Uzziah said to her, "All that you have said you have spoken with a good heart, and no one can deny your words.
Today is not the first time your wisdom has been shown; from the beginning of your days all the people have known your understanding, for the inclination of your heart is good.
But the people were very thirsty, and they forced us to do as we told them and to bind ourselves with an oath that we will not break.
So now pray for us, for you are a devout woman, and the Lord will send rain to fill our cisterns, and we will no longer faint."
Judith said to them, "Listen to me. I am going to do a thing that will go down through all generations to the sons of our race.
Stand at the gate tonight, and I will go out with my maid. Within the days after which you said you would surrender the city to our enemies, the Lord will deliver Israel by my hand.
But do not inquire into what I am doing, for I will not tell you until what I am doing is finished."
Uzziah and the rulers said to her, "Go in peace, and may the Lord God go before you to take vengeance on our enemies."
So they left the tent and went back to their posts.
